children: The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note rose to above 5.01% on Wednesday, the highest in 19 years, after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25bps.
The move was largely expected by financial markets after recent data pointed to high inflation, low unemployment, and strong consumer spending.
Projections by FOMC members pointed to one or two additional rate hikes by next year, consistent with upward revisions to forecasts on inflation and downward revisions to unemployment.
Besides higher inflation due to soaring energy prices, the Chairman Warsh also acknowledged that Treasuries have been pressured by competing for capital allocation with soaring corporate debt supply.

Still, longer-term maturities rose less than the shorter part of the curve as confidence that the Fed unanimously raised rates to fight inflation restored some credibility for the central bank, after Chairman Warsh had earlier downplayed the urgency of a higher funds rate to reign in price growth.

title: US 10-Year Yield Rises to 19-Year High
